newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's BBAG sees higher 1996 pretax.
newsitem.headline: Austria's BBAG sees higher 1996 pretax.

text.p: Austria's leading brewing group Oesterreichische Brau-Beteiligungs-AG (BBAG) said on Wednesday it would post a pre-tax profit of over one billion schillings in 1996, compared with 771 million in 1995.

"We expect our operating result to be 600 million schillings, the same level as 1995 would have been without the loss of 50 million from our Polish Coca Cola licence," chief executive Johannes Brandl told a news conference. The group's operating profit was 550 million schillings in 1995.
The company last year sold its Coca Cola franchises in Austria and Poland.
Group turnover was predicted to fall to 10 billion schillings in 1996, from 11.08 billion last year, which includes around one billion schillings from the franchise sales.
Brandl said BBAG's basic dividend for 1996 would remain unchanged at 15 schillings, but would not rule out the possibility of a bonus on top of that.
Brewer Brau Union AG, majority owned by BBAG, would pay a basic dividend of 22 schillings for 1996. In 1995 BBAG paid out a dividend of 17 schillings and Brau-Union 23 schillings.
Group beer sales fell 1.5 percent to 8.17 million hectolitres, hurt by a three percent fall in Austrian sales alone. Foreign beer sales rose 1.6 percent, with sales in Hungary climbing 0.9 percent.
"Our earnings developed particularly well in Hungarian breweries and in our property business," Brandl said.
Beer exports also saw new growth in the former Soviet Union and Yugoslavia.
Overall soft drink sales tumbled 3.9 percent, but fruit juice sales jumped 11.6 percent to 4.1 million hectolitres.
BBAG said it aimed to improve its growth through exports and acquisitions, faced with stagnating beer markets across Europe.
"We want to grow further, that means through exports and acquisitions, particularly in Central and Eastern Europe,"
Brandl said there was little scope for new acquisitions in Hungary but did not rule out future purchases in Romania.
The company plans to invest 1.7 billion schillings this year, against last year's 1.5 billion.
